A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PARCO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original HCVRP, OMDCPDP and FFSP experiments, including benchmark results, component ablations and scalability analyses in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark, generalization, ablation and timing results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4, with experimental details in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The stated decoder computation changes: v2 Equation (7) adds projected dynamic node features to the final pointer-logit keys, whereas v1 Equation (5) uses the encoded-node projection L. The core architecture and training objective remain. V2's 'learned' conflict priorities retain v1's High Probability rule rather than introducing a separate learned component.

E1.justification: All three task families remain, but real-world evaluation coverage is removed. V1 Appendix B.2.1 reports 32 Seoul-based instances for large-scale OMDCPDP and illustrates them in Figure 4. V2 Appendix B.2.2 instead reports generated generalization instances, with no retained Seoul evaluation.

E2.justification: V2 adds DPN to the evaluated HCVRP baselines and replaces CPLEX with Gurobi for FFSP. It also substantially expands the retained 18/24/30-machine FFSP comparisons: v1 Table 4 compares MatNet and PARCO, while v2 Table 1 additionally evaluates Random, SJF, GA and PSO in these configurations.

E3.justification: OMDCPDP's training agent range changes from 10–50 to 5–20, its in-distribution test size from 100 to 1000, and OR-Tools budgets from a uniform 300 seconds to size-dependent 30/60/300/600 seconds. FFSP's reported test size falls from 1000 to 100 generated instances; PARCO training for the larger-machine, 50-job comparisons changes from 20 to 150 epochs. V2 also adds 128-solution FFSP sampling evaluation.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 3(b) adds a without-communication control to FFSP decoding-step and training-time comparisons, and Section 5.3 reports a 4% conflict-rate reduction. Conversely, the First handler, size-separated communication/handler ablations and FFSP objective results without communication disappear. The central component and scalability questions remain.

E5.justification: V1 already shows error bars for communication ablations. V2 extends uncertainty bars to conflict-handler and FFSP step-count comparisons in Figure 3(b,c), whose corresponding v1 comparisons lacked them. Neither PDF explains the bars' statistical meaning or specifies training-run or seed counts.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised or replaced. Overlapping HCVRP objectives remain unchanged, but PARCO timings change: greedy N=60, M=3 goes from 0.12 to 0.04 seconds. OMDCPDP results are replaced under revised settings. V1's FFSP20 PARCO objective of 26.47 becomes 26.31 greedy, with a new sampled result of 24.78 under v2's changed test protocol. HCVRP N=80 results are removed; these changes do not establish a uniform same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 Equation (32) corrects the FFSP precedence-count constraint by moving the subtraction of 1 outside the inner sum over jobs. This changes the mathematical constraint rather than merely its notation. The remaining appendix problem formulations are largely retained.

C1.justification: V1's abstract, contributions and conclusion emphasize competitive performance against classical and neural methods. V2 strengthens the headline claim to outperforming state-of-the-art learning methods and makes generalization more prominent. The three architectural contributions and routing/scheduling scope remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds the limitation that PARCO cannot directly handle problems with an unspecified agent count, proposing agent-count search or prediction. It removes v1's proposed conflict-penalizing loss and local/population-search extensions, while retaining the explanation of fallback-step overhead in Section 4.6. Section 5.3 newly interprets communication as reducing training time through fewer decoding steps.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit masking and query-construction details, specifies the logit scale as 10, and adds baseline source attribution and an asset-license table. Reported software changes from PyTorch 2.4/Ubuntu 22.04.4 to PyTorch 2.5/Ubuntu 24.04. Some explicit 2D-Ptr and MAPDP hyperparameters are removed in favor of references. PARCO's code-release address is retained.

R1.justification: The literature discussion is substantially recast around types of autoregressive multi-agent construction. V2 adds decentralized routing comparisons, including Cao et al. (2022) and Park et al. (2023), and newer constrained-routing and speculative-decoding references. V1 Appendix C's connections to prioritized pathfinding, social navigation and automated priority heuristics disappear; some foundation-model discussion instead moves into Section 2.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much of the methodological narrative are rewritten. V2 reorganizes the method into seven subsections and separates experimental results from analysis. Appendix headings are simplified, the contents list and Additional Discussion section are removed, and a standalone limitations paragraph and impact statement are introduced.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text, enlarges and revises the architecture diagram, consolidates benchmark tables and separates generalization results. Component plots are redesigned, FFSP steps and training times receive a combined plot, and scalability becomes a standalone figure. The Seoul map is removed, the two appendix decoding diagrams become Figure 5(a,b), and a license table is added.

improvement.justification: V2 provides clearer organization, broader comparator coverage and an FFSP constraint correction. However, it removes the Seoul evaluation and some size-specific ablation evidence, reduces FFSP testing, and changes conditions behind many headline results without a matched comparison between protocols. These gains and losses leave the net effect on overall evidential strength and paper quality uncertain.
